1: This is the map for the whole programme. Every later module is a deep dive on one or two of these stages, so the goal today is breadth, not depth: everyone should leave able to name all seven stages in order and explain what goes wrong when one is skipped. Run time about two hours: 15 min intro and the flow, roughly 12 min per stage including its quick exercise, 15 min group exercise, 5 min close. Keep the per-stage exercises short and practical; the deep-dive modules go further.
2: Read the three outcomes aloud and tell the group they will be tested on the first one at the end, every person names the seven stages from memory. Ask people to keep their live role in mind and, at each stage, note one thing they did well and one thing they skipped.
3: Walk the seven stages left to right, top to bottom. For each one, ask “what breaks later if this stage is weak?”, a weak intake gives a weak shortlist, a skipped pre-close becomes a lost offer, no aftercare means no referral. Make the point that this is a loop, not a line: stage 7 feeds stage 1. Point out the module number under each stage so people know where the deep dive lives. About 10 minutes.
4: Stage one is where every placement starts. Ask the room: “Which of our current clients came from a warm intro, and which from a cold call?” Use the answer to make the point about referrals. Stress qualifying the client: a slow payer or an indecisive hiring manager costs you weeks. Quick role-play to close the stage (5 min): one person opens a first-touch BD call with a market insight, not a pitch; the partner gives feedback on whether it earned a second conversation. Full detail lives in Modules 05 and 06.
5: “Garbage in, garbage out.” Most failed searches can be traced back to a ten-minute intake call that should have been forty. Ask someone to share the last brief they took and test it against the six boxes live. Which box was empty? That gap is usually where the search stalled. Quick drill (5 min): run a mock qualification call and name the three most important open questions you still have at the end. Module 04 goes deep on grading and must-haves.
6: Compliance flag: we ask for a candidate’s target or expected package, never their current or past salary. NYC and many US states ban salary-history questions. For right to work, ask “Are you legally authorised to work in the US?” and “Will you now or in the future need visa sponsorship?”, don’t ask about citizenship or visa type. Quick drill (5 min): screen a mock CV against a live brief and list the first three questions you’d ask. Module 03 covers the full call flow and outreach.
7: Show a real submission email from the team (anonymised) next to a bare CV forward and ask which one the hiring manager is more likely to act on. The summary should answer three things: why this person, why now, and what the risk is. Setting a feedback deadline at submission is the first act of client control (Module 07). Quick drill (5 min): write a two-line submission summary for a candidate with an unconventional background.
8: The headline here is that client prep is as important as candidate prep and is the step average recruiters skip. On “send the weakest first”: only where it’s genuinely possible and the candidate is still credible for the role, never send someone you wouldn’t stand behind. Quick drill (5 min): role-play a pre-close call that includes one real objection to overcome. Module 08 has the full scripts.
9: Ask the room for a deal they lost at offer stage and work back: which earlier stage was weak? Almost always it’s a missed pre-close or a counteroffer nobody prepared for. Presenting the offer live matters because you hear the hesitation an email hides. Quick drill (5 min): talk a candidate through a counteroffer at the point of resignation. Module 09 covers counteroffers in full.
10: This is the stage that turns one placement into the next three. A 30-day call to the hiring manager is a BD call with a warm reason to ring. Ask everyone to put calendar reminders in for every current starter before they leave the room. Quick drill (5 min): draft a 30/60/90-day check-in message for a new starter.
11: This pulls together the seven quick drills from each stage. Walk the floor while pairs work and listen for the stage people skip most; it’s usually client prep or aftercare. In the debrief, collect the lowest-scoring stage from each pair on a whiteboard. The pattern tells you which deep-dive module the group needs next. Managers: pick up each person’s “one fix” in their next 1:1.
12: Test the first outcome now: go round the room and have each person name the seven stages in order from memory. Then each person reads out the one action they’ll do first. Managers should check all five actions at the next weekly 1:1.
13: Open the floor for questions. Remind the group the lifecycle is a loop: aftercare feeds business development. Point to Module 03, which goes deep on stage 3: finding, qualifying and engaging candidates.
